items.title: Johnny Lala Interview, 1960-03-15
items.q: Now, Custin Miller was in Paul with Paul Lightman.

ctx.x: Galen Barrow made some early attempts at jazz with his band. I guess with the sax section and all, there are some records around.

They're doing some jazz too. He started with that style and he's still going to. And I think it was pretty up too successful. Now, Custin Miller was in Paul with Paul Lightman. Yeah. Custin Miller. He played trombone, didn't he? Clarinet. Clarinet. Yeah. He was here last year. Yeah, he was here last year. Yeah, you told me that.

Is he the little fellow that was out there that was and we recorded him? Oh. We recorded him, John. He played some of the cutest stuff on clarinet. You know, we were just playing for the fun of it and he was there. It was that old style, but I mean it was a nice style. It wasn't a corny style. Well, he had a nice style. No, he had a nice style.

items.title: Johnny Lala Interview, 1958-09-24
items.q: But like, just like Paul White, we came along and made this symphonic, you know, with jazz.

ctx.x: How many cornets did you use with Shields? Two.

We had the first one, he's dead, Harry Shannon. Then I had, we had Henrikh Konek with us. And we had Dan Tyler playing sax. We had a wonderful little jazz band. And at that time we were, we were, you see, in them days, most of these bands would run around playing with nothing but chords. You know what I mean? But they'd stick on the chords and funny facts. But George, we played music. Then we used to mix it in. You know what I mean? And we harmonized, you see? Then they had that wind jam, you know what I mean?…
Who did he have in the rhythm section then?
